root_cause.text: `rtnl_fill_vfinfo()` in `net/core/rtnetlink.c` used an uninitialized stack `struct ifla_vf_broadcast` and only partially overwrote its 32-byte `broadcast` field with `dev->addr_len` bytes, so the remaining bytes were leaked to userspace via `nla_put()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(&vf_broadcast, 0, sizeof(vf_broadcast));` immediately before `memcpy(vf_broadcast.broadcast, dev->broadcast, dev->addr_len);`, and the CVE text states the struct was previously declared on the stack without initialization and then emitted with `nla_put(skb, IFLA_VF_BROADCAST, sizeof(vf_broadcast), &vf_broadcast)`, leaking uninitialized stack bytes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize `vf_broadcast` before filling its broadcast field to avoid leaking stale data in VF info output.
intent_record.what: In `rtnl_fill_vfinfo()`, a new `memset(&vf_broadcast, 0, sizeof(vf_broadcast));` call was inserted immediately before copying `dev->broadcast` into `vf_broadcast.broadcast`.
intent_record.how: This ensures the `vf_broadcast` structure is fully zero-initialized before only part of it is populated, preventing any leftover uninitialized bytes from being included in the data sent to userspace or other consumers.

candidates.rationale: This line only copies dev->addr_len bytes into a fixed-size broadcast field, leaving the rest of the stack-allocated struct uninitialized and leaking stale data when the whole struct is later sent to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies only dev->addr_len bytes into vf_broadcast.broadcast, leaving the rest of the fixed-size broadcast array uninitialized in the stack struct. Because the full struct is later exposed via nla_put(), the remaining bytes can leak stale kernel stack data to userspace.
